questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The city that I chose was very appealing to me and felt like a good place to broaden my knowledge of Japanese culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The workload and academic expectations on us as exchange students was overwhelming and accommodations were disgusting and sub par in every way. I wish I had known more about the host uni and been able to make a better informed decision when applying to study abroad.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Dorm supporters were helpful when it came to bureaucratic procedures. The first classes at uni were extremely information heavy with no translations for us non-japanese speakers.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As a neurodivergent student I was asked to come in for an hour long interview before classes started. I was asked questions about my challenges and then made to fill out an application stating that attendance can be difficult for me at times, and then sign it. I have no idea what happened after that as I received no further help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Ridiculously overwhelming and inconsiderate of our emotional state.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Two different dorms, Mitra-kan and International House. We were hoping to get rooms in Mitra-kan as that dorm has private toilets for each resident, but I guess something went wrong in communication between our two universities and we were not informed of the application deadline until it was too late and we had to settle for rooms at International House.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were two kitchens, one on the second floor (available to both sexes) and one on the third floor which was female only. The kitchens were in a very bad shape, everything was constantly sticky, it very quickly got crowded and other residents would take things without asking and leave a terrible mess. One resident got seriously injured because someone left a puddle of oil on the floor and just walked away. I never used the kitchen because of how disgusting it was and ended up using a ridiculous amount of money on Uber Eats and restaurants.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Don't do it if you like privacy and good hygiene. The shared toilets and showers were too disgusting to describe. It was not uncommon to walk in and find every single toilet with unflushed feces, urine and toilet paper on the floor, period blood on the toilet seats. The showers were cleaned every day by staff but as soon as they left, people would leave a flood of water and enough hair to make a wig on the floor.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Never again. Find a share-house or something if you value your mental health.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It would have been impossible to do on our own, but thankfully we had help from the dorm supporters. It was still a very tiring process though.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to go and register at the ward office and bring several forms and papers and then had to fill out and sign a bunch more papers at the ward office. We were also required to set up Japanese bank accounts in order to pay our dorm rent, but only for our last two months. Before then, we paid with bills that we brought to the convenience store and paid in cash. When the automatic bank transfer was supposed to happen in December, it didn't work and a man had to come from the bank and collect our rent in cash. Then we had to close our accounts at the bank before we left. We also had to visit the ward office again to pay our National Health Insurance. Extremely energy consuming.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Dorm supporters.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the electives that I wanted and I was very happy with each one.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The online process for the electives is quite easy. The Japanese classes are different as there seems to be no clear or understandable process for how they place you. Me and my fellow students from Copenhagen were initially placed in JEP 3, but after two or three classes (which we did ok in and were able to keep up), we received an email at night that we had been moved down to JEP 2 and would not be able to complain. It felt underhanded and uncomfortable. We were treated like children and had no say in our own programme structure. In the few classes that we did have in JEP 3, we were clearly targeted and constantly tested.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The electives were great. Japanese class was overwhelming and too work heavy.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Japanese class was level appropriate, but far too work heavy and stressful. I gave up half way through the semester. Japanese Technology was very easy and interesting. Media and arts and Pop Culture were more challenging, but also very interesting and rewarding. I learned a lot in those classes.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Polar opposites. Much less empathy and understanding of burn out and students such as myself with special needs. The coordinator who made me send the application for extra support was very passive aggressive, unhelpful and blamed my stress and mental anguish on me, rather than being understanding and trying to help me.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Japanese language (including core, listening through videos, reading comprehension and homeroom) and Japanese Technology, Japanese Pop Culture and Japanese Media and Arts.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Japanese Technology because its online and you dont need any previous knowledge on the subject, you just have to be active in class and interested. Japanese Media and Arts was fantastic and Danielly is an incredibly intelligent and empathetic instructor who taught us so much. Japanese Pop Culture was also a good course, but its popular, so the class is very big and it can be difficult to concentrate with so many people in the room.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Way too much money on food. There is also a need to carry cash everywhere.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The national health insurance.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were some nice field trips organized by the dorm supporters.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not sure but there were lots of things posted in the dorm.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sushiro. Shabu Shabu.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Get a color analysis if you have time. I wish I had the energy to take more trips around Japan. I only saw Kyoto and Tokyo.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The local people are kind and polite.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Probably adjusting to refined carbs and the fact that everything is sweet.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people are so kind. A woman chased me down the street to give me a bandaid for my blister.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Be superhumanly motivated and energetic. 2. Be ok with gross living quarters. 3. Remember to take care of yourself, even if you feel guilty for missing class etc.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't go to Ryukoku. You will have no time and energy for anything but school. Especially don't go if you are neurodivergent as you will receive zero help and support from R-Globe.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Sushiro.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Everything school and dorm related.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Do your research before picking a host uni. Don't just choose based on what city you would like to live in.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
